# Wolfenstein-style FPS

A single-level, first-person maze shooter in the spirit of 1992 — original,
procedurally generated, running on modern rendering. Built for an RTX 5080 at 1440p
and 120+ fps: real 3D geometry, not a raycaster.

**Every texture, sprite, font and sound is generated by code at load time.** The
repository contains no image, audio, or model files, and never will — that constraint
is the project's defining property, not an optimization.

## Playing it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
```

Or from a production build:

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

Uses WebGPU when the browser offers it, WebGL otherwise.

### Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| WASD | Move |
| Mouse | Look (pointer lock) |
| Shift | Sprint |
| Space / E | Interact — doors, secrets, pickups |
| Ctrl / LMB | Fire |
| 1 / 2 / 3 | Pistol / SMG / Chaingun |
| Esc | Release pointer |

## Checking it

```bash
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
npm run build       # production bundle
npm run test        # vitest — pure logic: grid, collision, pathing, doors, textures
npm run smoke       # headless Chromium: loads the game, asserts it actually renders
```

`npm run smoke` is the gate that matters. A browser game can compile perfectly and
show a black screen, so the harness loads the built page headlessly, fails on any
console error or uncaught exception, and reads `window.__diag` to confirm frames are
being drawn. Compiling is not passing.

## Building it

The project is defined entirely by the specs in [`specs/`](specs/), which an agentic
build factory (Ergane) consumes to dispatch implementation work. See
[`specs/README.md`](specs/README.md) for the spec index, the Work Graph grammar, and
operator notes on the model underneath.

- [`wolfenstein-prompt.md`](wolfenstein-prompt.md) — the original brief
- [`.specify/memory/constitution.md`](.specify/memory/constitution.md) — binding rules every build agent obeys
- [`factory.yaml`](factory.yaml) — what "green" means here
- `DECISIONS.md` — created during the build; records design forks and any fallback that was taken

## Status

Specs written, implementation not yet started. The `specs/` directory is complete and
validated against Ergane's Work Graph deriver; `src/` arrives with the first epic.
